## Structure of the book {.unnumbered}

Chapter [Introduction to R](introduction-to-r.qmd) gives a quick overview of R and its development tools.
Chapter [Install R & RStudio](install-r-and-rstudio.qmd) guides you through installing R and RStudio.
Chapter [Variables in R](variables-in-r.qmd) introduces variables and assignment.
Chapter [Data Types in R](data-types-in-r.qmd) introduces the types of values used in R.
Chapter [Vectors in R](vectors-in-r.qmd) covers vectors, coercion, operations and indexing.
Chapter [Dataframes in R](data-frames-in-r.qmd) covers creating and selecting rows and columns in data frames.
Chapter [Install & Update R Packages](install-update-r-packages.qmd) covers installing, loading and updating packages.
Chapter [RStudio Projects & Data Import](projects-import.qmd) covers portable paths and reading CSV and Excel files.
Chapter [Your First Visualization](first-plot.qmd) introduces base R and ggplot2 graphics.
Chapter [Your First Data Wrangling](first-wrangle.qmd) introduces dplyr verbs and the native pipe.
Chapter [Factors in R](factors-in-r.qmd) covers categorical data, levels and labels.
Chapter [Lists in R](lists-in-r.qmd) covers storing and extracting elements of different types.
Chapter [Getting Help in R](getting-help-in-r.qmd) shows where and how to ask for help and find documentation.
[About the Author](about-the-author.qmd) follows the chapters, and [Package management](appendix-package-management.qmd) collects reference material in an appendix.

## Software information {.unnumbered}

The R session information below shows the setup used to compile this book:

```{r session}
sessionInfo()
```

We do not add prompts (`>` and `+`) to R source code in this book. We comment out text output with two hashes `##` by default, as in the R session information above. This lets you copy and run the code, since R ignores the commented text output. Package names are in bold text (e.g., **rmarkdown**), and function names are followed by parentheses (e.g., `mean()`). The double-colon operator `::` means accessing an object from a package.
